concepts.title: Meaning of Design: Structural and Applied
concepts.definition: Design is planned creation for a purpose, not mere decoration; structural design grows out of the object itself -- fibre, yarn, weave, or the basic cut of a garment -- while applied design is laid on top through finishes, dyeing, printing, embroidery, trims and fasteners.
concepts.formula: design = structural base plus applied overlay
concepts.key_idea: True harmony arrives only when beauty is welded to usefulness; a pretty but unusable object is badly designed.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehe201.txt, Introduction and Design Analysis (approx lines 152-192)

concepts.title: Elements and Principles of Design
concepts.definition: The elements -- colour, texture, line, shape or form -- are the tools of the art, while the principles -- harmony, balance, rhythm, proportion and emphasis -- are the rules for blending those tools into an appealing whole.
concepts.formula: elements as tools worked through principles as rules
concepts.key_idea: A composition results when selected elements are placed by chosen principles in a given two or three dimensional space.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehe201.txt, design factors and composition (approx lines 193-197, 699-717)

concepts.title: Colour: Hue, Value and Intensity
concepts.definition: Colour is the eye's response to light reflected off a surface, read along three dimensions: hue, the colour's name; value, its lightness or darkness as tint or shade; and intensity or chroma, its brightness and purity, dulled by blending in the opposite hue.
concepts.formula: colour = hue plus value plus intensity
concepts.key_idea: The wheel starts from three primaries -- red, yellow, blue -- mixing to secondaries and six tertiaries, while white, black and greys stand apart as achromatic neutrals.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehe201.txt, colour theory and understanding colour (approx lines 211-280, 327-349)

concepts.title: Colour Schemes and Harmonies
concepts.definition: Related schemes share at least one hue -- monochromatic, achromatic, accented neutral and analogous -- while contrasting schemes set hues apart through complementary, split complementary, double complementary, analogous complementary and triadic pairings read off the colour wheel.
concepts.formula: scheme choice -- related shares a hue, contrasting opposes hues
concepts.key_idea: A scheme only proposes hues; the designer still decides values, intensities and quantities.

concepts.title: Texture in Fabrics and Dress
concepts.definition: Texture is what a material looks like, how it behaves and how it feels; in textiles it is fixed by the fibre content, yarn processing and type, construction technique, finishes and surface ornamentation, and in dress it must flatter the figure, silhouette and occasion.
concepts.formula: texture = sight plus behaviour plus touch
concepts.key_idea: Heavy bulky textures overpower a petite frame, so texture choices must serve the wearer's build.

solution_steps.explain: looks, behaves, feels

concepts.title: Line and Its Types
concepts.definition: A line joins two points and carries direction and mood: vertical lines stress height with a severe dignity, horizontal lines suggest width, calm and stability, diagonal lines dramatise by stretching or squeezing both, while curved lines from restrained arcs to circular sweeps read as soft, graceful and feminine.
concepts.formula: line types -- straight vertical, horizontal, diagonal plus curved restrained to circular
concepts.key_idea: Straight line dominance gives a masculine force; flowing curves lend grace and rhythm.

solution_steps.explain: up down, side to side, slanted -- each with its own illusion

concepts.title: Shapes, Forms and Patterns
concepts.section: Elements of Design: Shapes or Forms
concepts.definition: Connecting lines builds shapes, two dimensional on cloth or three dimensional on the body; the four basic groups are natural, stylised, geometric and abstract, and grouping shapes yields patterns whose placement or repeat finishes a fabric design.
concepts.formula: shapes from lines; patterns from grouped shapes
concepts.key_idea: In apparel, shape and form appear as silhouette, cut and detailing; in fabric, as drape, motif and repeat.
question_patterns: name the four basic groups of shapes in design

solution_steps.explain: copies of nature, simplified nature, ruler made figures, free forms
grouping one or several shape types sets the repeat of the design

concepts.title: Proportion and the Golden Mean
concepts.definition: Proportion governs how one part of a design relates to another and to the whole; the classical guide is the golden mean, which splits a garment in uneven ratios such as 3:5:8 or 5:8:13 at waistline, yoke and hemline, and extends to colour, texture and motif size as well.
concepts.formula: golden mean ratios -- 3 to 5 to 8 up to 5 to 8 to 13
concepts.key_idea: Unequal horizontal divisions slim the figure while equal halves shorten and widen it; a high waist bodice can hide abdominal fullness.

concepts.title: Balance in Dress
concepts.definition: Balance equals the visual weight on either side of a garment's centre, vertically and horizontally; formal balance mirrors the symmetrical body and feels stable though monotonous, informal balance evens unequal parts by placement, and radial balance flows out from a centre point.
concepts.formula: balance types -- formal plus informal plus radial
concepts.key_idea: Horizontal balance corrects figure problems, for instance a dark hue over a large area.

solution_steps.explain: equalised weight from the central point, checked both ways
mirror symmetry, adjusted placement, radiation from a hub

concepts.title: Emphasis and the Focal Point
concepts.definition: Emphasis plants the spot where the eye lands first -- through contrast of colour, unusual shape, line, detailing or accessories -- and smart dressing aims it at the face or at a figure strength while steering it away from a problem zone.
concepts.formula: emphasis = one dominant focal area per garment
concepts.key_idea: A bright belt celebrates a small waist, while a hip belt on full hips only advertises them.

solution_steps.explain: the area that captures the first glance

worked_examples.q: The spot where the eye lands first is called the what: focal point or hemline?

concepts.title: Rhythm in Design
concepts.definition: Rhythm repeats lines, colours or details so the eye travels easily across the garment; it arises through repetition of trims, gradation or cordation of motif sizes, radiation from gathers at waist or cuff, and parallelism of tucks or pleats.
concepts.formula: rhythm routes -- repetition plus gradation plus radiation plus parallelism
concepts.key_idea: Ordered movement of the eye is what turns scattered detail into visual unity.
question_patterns: what is rhythm in dress design

solution_steps.explain: organised repetition letting the eye flow
repetition, gradual size change, radiation from a centre, parallel placement

worked_examples.q: Repeating lines and details so the eye travels easily is called what: rhythm or silence?

concepts.title: Harmony and Composition
concepts.definition: Harmony is the agreement of every element -- shape matching shape, texture suiting texture across kurta, salwar and dupatta -- and a composition is the final artwork built by placing elements through chosen principles in a two or three dimensional space.
concepts.formula: harmony = all elements agreeing; composition = elements plus principles in a space
concepts.key_idea: A silk kurta with a cotton dupatta breaks textural harmony; one square pocket can break shape harmony of curved collar and cuffs.

solution_steps.explain: shape, texture and colour continuity across all garment areas
the deliberate placement of elements by selected principles

worked_examples.q: The agreement of every element in a design is called what: harmony or chaos?

concepts.title: Careers in Fabric and Apparel Design
concepts.section: Preparing for a Career and Scope
concepts.definition: The field splits into fabric design, which demands command of fibre characteristics, processing and dyeing behaviour, and apparel design; training runs from certificates and diplomas to bachelor degrees, and textile designers work in industry, fashion houses, design agencies or freelance, tracking trends ahead of the curve.
concepts.formula: career base -- fibre knowledge plus dyeing knowledge plus design principles
concepts.key_idea: Apparel textile designs turn over faster than furnishing designs, so trend awareness is a job requirement.

solution_steps.explain: fabric for many uses, apparel using many materials

concepts.title: Golden Mean Arithmetic
concepts.definition: When a garment divides on golden mean units, any part's share of the whole is its unit count over the combined units, scaled to a percentage -- the arithmetic behind a pleasing 3:5 blouse and skirt split.
concepts.key_idea: The 3:5 split gives the blouse 37.5 per cent of the whole; the shirt-pant 5:8 split gives the shirt about 38.5 per cent.

concepts.title: Grey Scale Position
concepts.definition: The value chart runs through eleven grades from black at zero to white at ten with grey as the mid value; a hue's distance below white is the white grade minus its own grade, telling whether it sits in shade or tint territory.
concepts.key_idea: Grades below five are shades approaching black, grades above five are tints approaching white.
